exact_statement: For a simply connected planar domain Omega with distinct boundary points a,b, take a delta-scaled honeycomb approximation with boundary endpoints a_delta,b_delta and a self-avoiding a_delta-to-b_delta path weighted proportionally to z_c^length, where z_c=1/sqrt(2+sqrt(2)). The related conjecture is convergence as delta tends to zero to chordal SLE_8/3 from a to b in Omega.
source: Bauerschmidt-Duminil-Copin-Goodman-Slade, Lectures on Self-Avoiding Walks, arXiv:1206.2092, Conjecture 1.5 and Section 3.3; https://arxiv.org/html/1206.2092
source_quote: For z=z_c, the random curve omega_delta converges to SLE_8/3
proof_or_counterexample: Direct primary-source scope check; not P0003's original fixed-length/free-endpoint statement and not a proof of convergence.
remaining_gap: No proved transfer from this chordal model to Grimmett's fixed-length free-endpoint question; both scaling-limit problems remain unproved in this packet.

exact_statement: Let H be the infinite hexagonal lattice and sample uniformly from the n-step self-avoiding walks that start at the origin, with no prescribed endpoint. Grimmett asks whether, after a suitable but unspecified spatial rescaling as n tends to infinity, their laws converge weakly to an SLE_8/3 random curve.
source: Geoffrey R. Grimmett, Selected problems in probability theory, arXiv:2205.07318v1, Question 2.2, PDF page 3; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.07318
source_quote: Does a uniformly distributed n-step SAW from the origin of H converge weakly
proof_or_counterexample: Read Question 2.2 and preceding definition of n-step SAWs in the primary PDF. The source does not specify scaling exponent, target SLE geometry or stopping rule, parametrization, or curve topology; these are not silently supplied from the related chordal conjecture.

remaining_gap: Current-open status still requires bounded recent-primary check; no equivalence to the variable-length chordal model is proved.

status: proved special case; independent review pending
exact_statement: For a fixed bounded planar domain approximated by finite honeycomb graphs H_delta with N_delta=O(delta^-2), let P_delta be any selected a_delta-to-b_delta SAW. Give each edge of P_delta weight z_c and every other edge weight z_c exp(-delta^-4). The product-weight SAW measure has the exact domain Markov property for every delta, yet P(omega=P_delta)->1. If P_delta converges to a deterministic simple curve, so do these measures; they cannot converge to chordal SLE_8/3.
assumptions: Finite honeycomb subgraphs, one selected SAW P_delta, N_delta<=C delta^-2, z_c=(2+sqrt(2))^-1/2, product edge weights; selected curves may be chosen in a straight honeycomb corridor in a fixed rectangle.
source: owner-own-work; source for SAW target: arXiv:1206.2092 Conjecture 1.5; finite-volume Markov factorization derived here
proof_or_counterexample: For any realized prefix, its product weight cancels and suffix weights are those of a SAW in the graph with visited prefix vertices removed. Every omega!=P_delta uses an off-P_delta edge, hence has weight at most exp(-delta^-4) since z_c<1. There are at most 3^(N_delta+1) SAWs, while weight(P_delta)=z_c^L with L<=N_delta-1. Therefore P(omega!=P_delta)<=3^(N_delta+1) z_c^(-N_delta) exp(-delta^-4)=exp(-delta^-4+O(delta^-2))->0. A deterministic curve law differs from nondegenerate Brownian-driven SLE_8/3.
independent_reviewer: w407 requested in review packet; no verdict yet
remaining_gap: This refutes only the bridge from domain Markov property (even with honeycomb support and baseline critical fugacity) to SLE. Edge-dependent factors are absent from P0003's uniform-fugacity model, so it gives no counterexample to P0003.

status: independently checked proof of abstract special case
exact_statement: On a honeycomb patch, the complete local midpoint relation plus bounded fields and fixed boundary data does not force a continuous local limit: a unit six-edge cycle mode can make two midpoints at distance sqrt(3)*delta/2 differ by one while preserving all vertex equations and boundary values.
assumptions: All three incident midpoint values included at each honeycomb vertex; abstract complex fields, not necessarily SAW observables; a complete face tends to a fixed interior point.
source: w402 ATTEMPT.md, Lemma 2 and Proposition 3; primary local relation Duminil-Copin--Smirnov arXiv:1007.0575
proof_or_counterexample: For counterclockwise face edges v_j->v_(j+1), H(p_j)=delta/(v_(j+1)-v_j), zero elsewhere. Incoming and outgoing vertex terms cancel as -delta/2+delta/2. Constant field 1 also solves the complete local relation. At a face edge and third edge at one vertex, (1+H) values differ by |H|=1 while their midpoints are sqrt(3)*delta/2 apart. Hence locally uniform convergence to a continuous field is impossible.
remaining_gap: Physical SAW observables occupy a special combinatorial subset of these fields; this abstract obstruction does not prove nonconvergence of them or solve P0003.

exact_statement: There is a sequence of self-avoiding honeycomb paths in one fixed domain, with two distinct boundary endpoints and uniformly bounded speed, converging uniformly to a trace containing a macroscopic rectangular loop. Thus tightness and even uniform convergence of simple discrete paths do not alone ensure a simple limiting trace.
assumptions: Even N>=8, mesh 1/N, seven-route construction in w403 INDEPENDENT.md; deterministic path laws; not the uniform critical SAW ensemble.
source: w403 INDEPENDENT.md and check_honeycomb_pinch.py; reproduced from a copy in w404/verify_pinch.py
proof_or_counterexample: Independently checked parity and disjoint route regions; seven edge counts sum to 22N-12. On vertical routes with K row advances and 2K-1 edges, vertical progress differs from synchronized linear progress by <=1/K, so y error <=2/N; all route x errors <=2sqrt(3)/N. Thus uniform Euclidean error <=4/N, improving stated 5/N. The limiting anchors visit (0,0),(0,3),(sqrt(3),3),(sqrt(3),0),(0,0), a nontrivial closed rectangle. Exact-rational reproduction passed 5 N values (8,16,32,64,128), 5401 vertices, 0.191s; command python -X utf8 ~/brain_workers/w404/verify_pinch.py.
remaining_gap: w403 introduction calls the chordal model P0003; correct target is Grimmett fixed-length free-endpoint question. The constructed deterministic paths do not have the target law and do not refute it.

exact_statement: For n=1 and critical loop weight z=1/sqrt(3), the honeycomb O(1) loop model corresponds to the Ising model, and its boundary interface has a proved SLE_3 limit. The existing C0096 math-brain node's parenthetical 'site percolation, Smirnov' at this critical point is inconsistent with the cited source and should be replaced by 'critical Ising interface, SLE_3'. This is a correction to a related source card, not a solution of P0003.
assumptions: n=1, z=1/sqrt(3), boundary-to-boundary loop-model interface in the source's setup
source: Bauerschmidt-Duminil-Copin-Goodman-Slade, arXiv:1206.2092 Section 3.4 before Conjecture 3.7; https://arxiv.org/html/1206.2092 ; existing card math-brain-build/export/population/nodes.jsonl:2804
source_quote: For n=1 and z=1/sqrt(3), it has been proved that the interface converges to SLE_3
proof_or_counterexample: Primary source explicitly says n=1 corresponds to the Ising model and gives SLE_3 at z=1/sqrt(3); the stored C0096 statement instead says site percolation at that critical point. Direct source-versus-card contradiction.
remaining_gap: Reviewer should check the precise Ising boundary condition before applying the correction to the existing card; no live store edit made.

status: independently checked proof of abstract boundary problem
exact_statement: For prescribed complex boundary midpoint values g on a finite honeycomb patch, let b_v be their contribution to the full vertex relation. Interior midpoint solutions to BJ=-b exist exactly when each component C of the internal graph satisfies sum_(v in C)b_v=0; when they exist their affine dimension is |E|-|V|+c, including isolated vertices.
assumptions: All three incident midpoint positions included at each vertex, internal edges have nonzero displacement, boundary values fixed, arbitrary complex fields.
source: w402 ATTEMPT.md Lemma 1; local relation arXiv:1007.0575 Lemma 1 equation (1)
proof_or_counterexample: Orient internal edges and set J_e=(v-u)F(p_e)/2. Then L_v=(BJ)_v+b_v. Summing BJ over each component gives zero, proving necessity. On each component, delete one row from a spanning-tree incidence submatrix; its determinant is +/-1, so rank B=|V|-c and image B is exactly the componentwise zero-sum vectors. Rank-nullity gives affine dimension |E|-|V|+c. An isolated vertex has no internal edge and is solvable exactly when b_v=0, with dimension zero.
remaining_gap: This is algebra for arbitrary fields; it does not give regularity of the physical SAW observable or P0003 convergence.

exact_statement: If P_n converges weakly to P in the uniform topology on continuous curves, and E(r,q) is the event of a pair of times with endpoint separation at most r but intervening excursion diameter at least q, then P has no nonconstant self-return almost surely iff for every q>0, lim_(r downarrow 0) limsup_n P_n(E(r,q))=0.
assumptions: Probability laws on C([0,1],C) with uniform topology; r>=0, q>0; constant waiting intervals allowed.
source: w403 ATTEMPT.md, exact additional criterion; owner-own-work
proof_or_counterexample: E(r,q) is closed by compactness of witness times and continuity of endpoint distance and subcurve diameter; intersection as r decreases to zero is E(0,q). The closed-set Portmanteau inequality proves the forward implication. For the converse use open U(r,q) with strict inequalities: E(0,2q) subset U(r,q) subset E(r,q), and open-set Portmanteau gives P(E(0,2q))<=liminf_n P_n(E(r,q)). Let r down to zero and take countably many q=1/k.
remaining_gap: No estimate of E(r,q) is proved for uniform fixed-length honeycomb SAW; criterion alone supplies no SLE identification or P0003 proof.

exact_statement: For 0<epsilon<1, c_n=1 and a_n=1+epsilon*(-1)^n are nonnegative; their generating functions satisfy A(z)/C(z)->1 as real z tends to 1 from below, but a_n/c_n oscillates between 1+epsilon and 1-epsilon.
assumptions: 0<epsilon<1, real z in (0,1), ordinary power series about zero; abstract sequences only.
source: w401 ATTEMPT.md and CLAIMS.jsonl P0003-COEFF-005; owner-own-work
proof_or_counterexample: C(z)=sum z^n=1/(1-z); A(z)=C(z)+epsilon sum (-z)^n=1/(1-z)+epsilon/(1+z). Therefore A/C=1+epsilon(1-z)/(1+z)->1. The coefficient ratio is exactly 1+epsilon(-1)^n, with distinct even and odd subsequential limits. Positivity holds since 0<epsilon<1.
remaining_gap: Only refutes coefficient inference from a real-axis generating-function ratio; supplies no SAW asymptotics, complex-neighborhood transfer theorem, or P0003 proof.
